title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Canonical Fixes (Playbook)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the list of top support issues with canonical fixes. It is intended for engineers, technical writers, and support/solutions teams who produce or maintain dev-facing content for Redwood Inference.

Goals
- Produce consistent, high-quality developer docs that reduce onboarding time and support load.
- Provide canonical, reviewed code examples and troubleshooting steps to speed time-to-resolution.
- Maintain a repeatable publishing and review process for the docs site.
- Track top support issues and ensure a single canonical fix is available for each.

Audience
- SDK engineers and owners
- Developer advocates and technical writers
- Support engineers and solutions architects
- Product managers responsible for API/SDK surface changes

Document Types (what we publish)
1) SDK Guides
   - Purpose: detailed reference and how-tos for each supported SDK (Python, Node, Go, Java).
   - Structure: Quick start, auth, core primitives (client, requests, streaming), error handling, advanced usage (batching, caching), migration guide, API reference links.

2) Quickstarts & Templates
   - Purpose: 5–15 minute examples for common flows (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking).
   - Deliverables: language-specific quickstarts, minimal Docker examples, k8s manifest template for local testing, sample prompts.

3) API Examples
   - Purpose: compact, copy-paste examples demonstrating idiomatic usage patterns and recommended defaults (timeouts, retries, backoff).

4) Docs-site Operating Procedures
   - Purpose: how to publish, review, label, and retire content. Includes metrics and SLAs for doc reviews and post-release followup.

5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes
   - Purpose: triaged list of recurring support tickets mapped to canonical doc fixes and code snippets.

SDK Guide Template (required fields)
- Title (H1)
- Short intro (1-2 sentences)
- Prerequisites (account, API key, SDK version)
- Quickstart (copy-paste code)
- Concepts & primitives (bulleted sub-sections)
- Error handling & SLOs (recommended retry/backoff)
- Migration notes (version changes)
- Examples (links to quickstarts)
- Tests (how to run local integration tests)
- Ownership & reviewers

Example Quickstart (Python)
- Prereqs: Python 3.10+, pip, Redwood API key (export REDWOOD_API_KEY)
- Install: pip install redwood-sdk
- Minimal example:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate("Translate to French: 'Welcome to Redwood!'")
print(resp.text)
```

API Example (Node - streaming)
- Notes: use streaming for UI-first experiences to reduce TTFB. Set chunk_size=512 for mobile apps.

```javascript
import { Redwood } from 'redwood-js'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1.0', messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the release notes.'}] })
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta)
}
```

Docs-site Operating Procedures (how we publish)
1) Drafting
   - Create or update a JSON doc in confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates; follow SDK Guide Template.
   - Add 'devex' and language labels.
2) Review
   - Assign two reviewers (one SDK owner, one doc reviewer).
   - Reviews must complete within 5 business days for minor changes, 10 business days for major changes.
3) Staging and smoke tests
   - Deploy to docs staging site. Run smoke tests: code snippets lint, copy-paste examples execute (CI job: docs/quickstart-smoke).
4) Publish
   - Merge and tag the doc with release version (e.g., docs:v2026-02). Notify #devex channel.
5) Post-publish followup
   - Monitor telemetry for 72 hours: page views, click-to-copy rates, and new support tickets linked to the page.

Ownership
- Each doc must declare an owner in the front-matter (owner_team + author). Owners must respond to doc issues within 3 business days.

Review Checklist (required before publishing)
- [ ] Title and short intro present
- [ ] Prereqs and supported SDK versions listed
- [ ] Copy-paste examples tested in CI
- [ ] Error handling / retry guidance included
- [ ] Security notes (PII handling, API keys) included if applicable
- [ ] Labels and related_pages populated
- [ ] Owner and reviewers assigned

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (examples)
1) Authentication failures (expired/incorrect API key)
   - Symptom: HTTP 401 from SDK or API; users often paste whole key with quotes.
   - Canonical fix: Document snippet and CLI check:

```bash
# Verify env var is set and contains no surrounding quotes
echo "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | sed -n '1p'
# If value is quoted, remove quotes in your shell or key store
```
   - Doc: add troubleshooting section to all SDK guides and the top-level "Authentication" page.

2) Slow first-token latency in streaming chat
   - Symptom: UI waits > 1s for first token on cold connections.
   - Canonical fix: Recommend HTTP/2 or WebSocket streaming, set server-side keepalive, and use client preflight for model warming. Example config:

| Setting | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| connection_keepalive | 30s | Keep connections alive behind LB to avoid TLS handshake cost |
| stream_chunk_size | 512 | Mobile: smaller chunks; Desktop: 1024 |

3) Batching misconfiguration leads to 429s on Dedicated
   - Symptom: High 429 rate when multiple routes use same capacity pool.
   - Canonical fix: Provide example routing policy that isolates high-throughput routes into separate pools and set per-route concurrency limits. Add sample YAML for Dedicated routing: 

```yaml
route:
  name: support-search
  model: semantic-embed-1
  pool: customer-intent-pool
  concurrency_limit: 200
  timeout_ms: 20000
```

4) Unexpected model regressions after rollout
   - Symptom: Quality alerts triggered after model upgrade.
   - Canonical fix: Include a standard rollback play in all model rollout docs; link to evals harness. Steps:
   1. Pause rollout
   2. Re-route X% back to previous model version
   3. Run prompt set diffs and publish a regression ticket if delta > threshold

Canonical Fix Ownership and Tracking
- All canonical fixes must be referenced by an issue in the support tracker (prefix: DOCFIX-). Support and DevEx engineers tag new recurring issues and assign DOCFIX tickets. The owner is responsible for implementing the doc change within 5 business days for P1/P2 issues.

Examples & Canonical Snippets (copy-paste)
- Exponential backoff helper (Python):

```python
import time
from functools import wraps

def retry_backoff(max_retries=3, base_delay=0.5):
    def deco(f):
        @wraps(f)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            for i in range(max_retries):
                try:
                    return f(*args, **kwargs)
                except Exception as e:
                    if i == max_retries - 1:
                        raise
                    time.sleep(base_delay * 2 ** i)
        return wrapper
    return deco
```

Metrics & Success criteria
- Decrease in average time-to-first-successful-call for new users (target: < 15 minutes)
- Reduction in support tickets attributed to "docs" by 30% quarter-over-quarter
- 95% of quickstarts have passing smoke tests in CI
